e|a bit expensive.text: This shirt is a bit expensive for me.
e|a bit expensive.en: This shirt costs more money than I want to pay.
e|a bit expensive.ko: 이 셔츠는 내가 내고 싶은 것보다 좀 비싸요.

e|a bit expensive.text: I like this one, but it is a bit expensive.
e|a bit expensive.en: I like this, but the price is high.

e|a bit expensive.text: It looks nice, but it is a bit expensive.
e|a bit expensive.en: It looks good, but the price is high.

e|a blessing in disguise.text: Losing my wallet was actually a blessing in disguise because someone found it and returned it with everything inside.
e|a blessing in disguise.en: Losing my wallet turned out well because someone found it and returned it with everything inside.
e|a blessing in disguise.ko: 지갑을 잃어버렸는데 누군가가 모든 것이 그대로인 채로 찾아서 돌려줘서 오히려 좋은 일이었다.

e|a blessing in disguise.text: Getting stuck in traffic was a blessing in disguise since I missed the heavy rain at my destination.
e|a blessing in disguise.en: Getting stuck in traffic ended up being good because I avoided the heavy rain when I arrived.
e|a blessing in disguise.ko: 교통 체증에 걸렸지만 도착했을 때 큰비를 피할 수 있어서 오히려 좋은 일이었다.

e|a blessing in disguise.text: Not getting that job was a blessing in disguise because I found something even better later.
e|a blessing in disguise.en: Not getting that job turned out to be good because I found a better one afterwards.
e|a blessing in disguise.ko: 그 일자리를 얻지 못했지만 나중에 더 좋은 것을 찾을 수 있어서 오히려 잘 된 일이었다.

e|a grey area.text: Whether that's allowed or not is kind of a grey area.
e|a grey area.en: It's unclear whether that's allowed or not.

e|a grey area.text: The rules about working from home are still a grey area at my company.
e|a grey area.en: The rules about working from home are not clear at my company.
e|a grey area.ko: 우리 회사에서는 재택근무에 대한 규정이 아직 명확하지 않다.

e|a grey area.text: Is borrowing someone’s charger at work a grey area, or is it okay?
e|a grey area.en: Is borrowing someone’s charger at work unclear, or is it allowed?
e|a grey area.ko: 직장에서 다른 사람의 충전기를 빌리는 것이 애매한지, 아니면 괜찮은지 궁금하다.

e|a little cheaper.text: I wish my rent was a little cheaper.
e|a little cheaper.en: I want my rent to be less expensive.
e|a little cheaper.ko: 내 집세가 조금 더 쌌으면 좋겠어요.

e|a little cheaper.text: This shirt is nice, but do you have one a little cheaper?
e|a little cheaper.en: This shirt is good, but do you have a less expensive one?
e|a little cheaper.ko: 이 셔츠 좋지만, 조금 더 싼 거 있어요?

e|a little cheaper.text: I am looking for something a little cheaper.
e|a little cheaper.en: I want to find something that costs less.
e|a little cheaper.ko: 저는 좀 더 저렴한 것을 찾고 있어요.

e|a tight deadline.text: We’re working under a tight deadline, so let’s focus and get this done.
e|a tight deadline.en: We have very little time to finish this, so let’s concentrate and complete it.
e|a tight deadline.ko: 우리는 시간이 거의 없으니 집중해서 이 일을 끝내자.

e|a tight deadline.text: Sorry, I can’t meet for lunch today because I’m on a tight deadline.
e|a tight deadline.en: I can’t have lunch with you today because I have to finish my work quickly.
e|a tight deadline.ko: 오늘은 점심을 같이 못 먹겠어, 일이 급해서.

e|a tight deadline.text: Have you ever had to finish a big project with a tight deadline?
e|a tight deadline.en: Did you ever have to complete a large project in a very short amount of time?
e|a tight deadline.ko: 아주 짧은 시간 안에 큰 프로젝트를 끝내야 했던 적 있어?

e|are you free on.text: Hi, are you free on Friday night?
e|are you free on.en: Do you have time on Friday night?

e|are you free on.text: Are you free on Sunday to go for a walk?
e|are you free on.en: Do you have time on Sunday to go for a walk?

e|are you free on.text: Are you free on Thursday for a quick call?
e|are you free on.en: Do you have time on Thursday for a short call?

e|arguably.text: This is arguably the best pizza place in town.
e|arguably.en: This might be the best pizza place in town.
e|arguably.ko: 여기가 아마 이 동네에서 가장 맛있는 피자집일 거야.

e|arguably.text: Arguably, that movie changed how people see animation.
e|arguably.en: Some people say that movie changed how people see animation.
e|arguably.ko: 어떤 사람들은 그 영화가 사람들이 애니메이션을 보는 방식을 바꿨다고 해.

e|arguably.text: He's arguably the fastest runner on the team.
e|arguably.en: He might be the fastest runner on the team.
e|arguably.ko: 그가 팀에서 가장 빠른 주자일 수도 있어.

e|as long as.text: You can borrow my bike as long as you bring it back by tomorrow.
e|as long as.en: You can borrow my bike if you return it by tomorrow.
e|as long as.ko: 내일까지 돌려준다면 내 자전거를 빌릴 수 있어.

e|as long as.text: We can watch the movie as long as everyone finishes their homework first.
e|as long as.en: We can watch the movie if everyone finishes their homework first.
e|as long as.ko: 모두가 숙제를 먼저 끝낸다면 영화를 볼 수 있어.

e|as long as.text: As long as the weather stays nice, we’ll have the picnic outside.
e|as long as.en: If the weather stays nice, we’ll have the picnic outside.
e|as long as.ko: 날씨가 계속 좋다면 우리는 밖에서 소풍을 할 거야.

e|as soon as possible.text: Please call me back as soon as possible.
e|as soon as possible.en: Please call me back very quickly.
e|as soon as possible.ko: 최대한 빨리 저에게 다시 전화해 주세요.

e|as soon as possible.text: Let me know your answer as soon as possible.
e|as soon as possible.en: Tell me your answer very quickly.

e|as soon as possible.text: Please finish your homework as soon as possible.
e|as soon as possible.en: Please finish your homework very quickly.

e|be that as it may.text: Be that as it may, we still have to finish the project by tomorrow.
e|be that as it may.en: Even though that is true, we still have to finish the project by tomorrow.
e|be that as it may.ko: 그렇다 하더라도, 우리는 여전히 내일까지 프로젝트를 끝내야 해.

e|be that as it may.text: Be that as it may, I think we should try again next time.
e|be that as it may.en: Even if that's the case, I think we should try again next time.
e|be that as it may.ko: 그렇다 하더라도, 나는 우리가 다음 번에 다시 시도해야 한다고 생각해.

e|be that as it may.text: Be that as it may, she always finds a way to help out.
e|be that as it may.en: Even if that's the case, she always finds a way to help out.
e|be that as it may.ko: 그렇다 하더라도, 그녀는 항상 도울 방법을 찾아.

e|bear in mind.text: Just bear in mind that the store closes early on Sundays.
e|bear in mind.en: Remember that the store closes early on Sundays.
e|bear in mind.ko: 일요일에는 가게가 일찍 문을 닫는다는 점을 기억하세요.

e|bear in mind.text: Bear in mind, tickets might sell out quickly for that concert.
e|bear in mind.en: Remember, tickets might sell out quickly for that concert.
e|bear in mind.ko: 그 콘서트 표가 빨리 매진될 수 있다는 점을 기억하세요.

e|bear in mind.text: Bear in mind that your umbrella is still in my car.
e|bear in mind.en: Remember that your umbrella is still in my car.
e|bear in mind.ko: 네 우산이 아직 내 차에 있다는 것을 기억해.

e|beside the point.text: Whether it rains tomorrow is beside the point right now.
e|beside the point.en: Whether it rains tomorrow doesn’t matter right now.
e|beside the point.ko: 내일 비가 오는지 여부는 지금 중요하지 않아.

e|beside the point.text: Your favorite color is beside the point in this discussion.
e|beside the point.en: Your favorite color is not important in this discussion.
e|beside the point.ko: 네가 좋아하는 색깔은 이 논의에서 중요하지 않아.

e|beside the point.text: That excuse is beside the point because the mistake already happened.
e|beside the point.en: That excuse doesn’t matter because the mistake already happened.
e|beside the point.ko: 그 변명은 이미 실수가 일어났으니까 중요하지 않아.

e|by and large.text: By and large, the weather here is pretty mild all year.
e|by and large.en: Overall, the weather here is pretty mild all year.
e|by and large.ko: 전반적으로 이곳의 날씨는 일 년 내내 꽤 온화해요.

e|by and large.text: By and large, people seemed happy with the new changes.
e|by and large.en: Generally, people seemed happy with the new changes.
e|by and large.ko: 대체로 사람들은 새로운 변화에 만족하는 것 같았어요.

e|by and large.text: By and large, I try to eat healthy during the week.
e|by and large.en: For the most part, I try to eat healthy during the week.
e|by and large.ko: 대체로 나는 평일에는 건강하게 먹으려고 해요.

e|by the way.text: By the way, do you have an umbrella?
e|by the way.en: Also, do you have an umbrella?

e|by the way.text: By the way, your shoes look nice.
By the way, I saw your book on the table.
e|by the way.en: Also, I saw your book on the table.
e|by the way.ko: 그런데 네 책이 탁자 위에 있었어.

e|come up with.text: I need to come up with a gift for my friend's birthday.
e|come up with.en: I have to think of a present for my friend's birthday.
e|come up with.ko: 친구 생일 선물로 뭘 할지 생각해야 해.

e|come up with.text: She always manages to come up with funny stories.
e|come up with.en: She is always able to think of funny stories.
e|come up with.ko: 그녀는 항상 재미있는 이야기를 생각해 낸다.

e|come up with.text: How did you come up with that idea for the project?
e|come up with.en: How did you think of that idea for the project?

e|excuse me.text: Excuse me, can you help me?
Excuse me, where is the bus stop?
Excuse me, what time is it?

e|fair enough.text: You can’t come tonight? Fair enough.
e|fair enough.en: You cannot come tonight? I understand.
e|fair enough.ko: 오늘 밤에 올 수 없다고? 알겠어.

e|fair enough.text: It is too expensive for you? Fair enough.
e|fair enough.en: It costs too much for you? I understand.

e|fair enough.text: You want to go home early? Fair enough.
e|fair enough.en: You want to leave early? I understand.

e|figure it out.text: Let me try to figure it out.
e|figure it out.en: Let me try to find the answer.

e|figure it out.text: We need to figure it out before lunch.
e|figure it out.en: We need to solve it before lunch.

e|figure it out.text: It is hard, but I will figure it out.
e|figure it out.en: It is hard, but I will find the answer.
e|figure it out.ko: 이건 어렵지만, 내가 답을 찾을 거야.

e|for here or to go.text: Hi, for here or to go?
e|for here or to go.en: Do you want to eat here or take your food with you?

e|for here or to go.text: Is your coffee for here or to go?
e|for here or to go.en: Will you drink your coffee here, or take it out?
e|for here or to go.ko: 커피를 여기서 마실 건가요, 아니면 가져가실 건가요?

e|for here or to go.text: Let me know if your order is for here or to go.
e|for here or to go.en: Tell me if you want to eat here or take it away.
e|for here or to go.ko: 주문이 여기서 먹는 건지, 포장하는 건지 알려주세요.

e|for the record.text: Just for the record, I never agreed to that plan.
e|for the record.en: To be clear, I never agreed to that plan.
e|for the record.ko: 분명히 말하지만, 나는 그 계획에 동의한 적 없어.

e|for the record.text: For the record, I do like pineapple on pizza.
e|for the record.en: Just so you know, I do like pineapple on pizza.
e|for the record.ko: 참고로, 나는 피자에 파인애플 넣는 것을 좋아해.

e|for the record.text: For the record, I finished my part of the project yesterday.
e|for the record.en: Just to make it clear, I finished my part of the project yesterday.
e|for the record.ko: 분명히 하자면, 나는 어제 내 프로젝트 부분을 끝냈어.

e|for the time being.text: Let's keep the windows closed for the time being.
e|for the time being.en: Let's keep the windows closed for now.

e|for the time being.text: I'm staying with my brother for the time being.
e|for the time being.en: I'm living at my brother's place temporarily.
e|for the time being.ko: 나는 당분간 내 남동생 집에 머무르고 있어.

e|for the time being.text: For the time being, we don't need to buy more milk.
e|for the time being.en: Right now, we don't need to buy more milk.
e|for the time being.ko: 당분간 우유를 더 살 필요 없어.

e|get back to me.text: If you know the answer, get back to me.
e|get back to me.en: Let me know the answer when you find it.

e|get back to me.text: Get back to me when you have the details.
e|get back to me.en: Tell me when you have the information.
e|get back to me.ko: 자세한 내용을 알게 되면 나에게 알려줘.

e|get back to me.text: Please get back to me after you talk to your boss.
e|get back to me.en: Let me know after you speak with your boss.

e|good morning.en: Hello, how do you feel today?

e|good morning.text: Good morning, it is sunny today.
e|good morning.en: Hello, the sun is out today.

e|good morning.text: Good morning, did you sleep well?
e|good morning.en: Hello, did you have a good sleep?

e|have a nice day.text: Thank you for your help. Have a nice day.
e|have a nice day.en: Thanks for helping. Have a good day.

e|have a nice day.text: See you later. Have a nice day.
e|have a nice day.en: See you later. Have a good day.

e|have you ever been.text: Have you ever been to a big concert?
e|have you ever been.en: Did you go to a big music show before?

e|have you ever been.text: Have you ever been late for class?
e|have you ever been.en: Did you arrive late to class before?

e|have you ever been.text: Have you ever been on a boat?
e|have you ever been.en: Did you ride a boat before?

e|having said that.text: I’m not a big fan of spicy food; having said that, I do like a little bit of chili now and then.
e|having said that.en: I don’t usually like spicy food, but sometimes I enjoy a little chili.
e|having said that.ko: 나는 매운 음식을 별로 좋아하지 않지만, 가끔은 고추를 조금 즐긴다.

e|having said that.text: The weather is cold today; having said that, it’s actually quite nice for a walk.
e|having said that.en: It’s cold today, but it’s still nice for a walk.

e|having said that.text: This movie is long; having said that, it never feels boring.
e|having said that.en: The movie is long, but it doesn’t feel boring.
e|having said that.ko: 이 영화는 길지만 지루하게 느껴지지 않는다.

e|how about you.text: I like this game, how about you?
e|how about you.en: I like this game, do you like it too?
e|how about you.ko: 나는 이 게임이 좋아, 너는 어때?

e|how about you.text: I am not hungry, how about you?
e|how about you.en: I am not hungry, are you hungry?

e|how about you.text: I can ride a bike, how about you?
e|how about you.en: I can ride a bike, can you do it too?
e|how about you.ko: 나는 자전거를 탈 수 있어, 너는 어때?

e|how long does it take.text: How long does it take to walk to the park?
e|how long does it take.en: I want to know the time needed to walk to the park.
e|how long does it take.ko: 공원까지 걸어서 얼마나 걸리는지 알고 싶어요.

e|how long does it take.text: How long does it take to cook rice?
e|how long does it take.en: I want to know the time needed to cook rice.
e|how long does it take.ko: 쌀을 요리하는 데 얼마나 걸리는지 알고 싶어요.

e|how long does it take.text: How long does it take to learn to swim?
e|how long does it take.en: I want to know the time needed to learn to swim.
e|how long does it take.ko: 수영을 배우는 데 얼마나 걸리는지 알고 싶어요.

e|how much is this.text: How much is this for one apple?
e|how much is this.en: What is the price for one apple?

e|how much is this.text: Hi, how much is this small bag?
e|how much is this.en: Hello, what is the price of this small bag?

e|how much is this.text: How much is this toy on the shelf?
e|how much is this.en: What is the price of this toy on the shelf?

e|how was your weekend.en: Hello, did you have a good weekend?

e|how was your weekend.text: How was your weekend at the lake?
e|how was your weekend.en: Did you have a good weekend at the lake?

e|how was your weekend.text: How was your weekend with your family?
e|how was your weekend.en: Did you have a good weekend with your family?

e|in hindsight.text: In hindsight, I should have packed an umbrella today.
e|in hindsight.en: Now that I think about it, I should have brought an umbrella today.
e|in hindsight.ko: 지나고 보니 오늘 우산을 챙겼어야 했어요.

e|in hindsight.text: In hindsight, staying up late last night was a bad idea.
e|in hindsight.en: Looking back, staying up late last night wasn't a good decision.
e|in hindsight.ko: 돌이켜보니 어젯밤에 늦게까지 깨어 있었던 건 좋지 않은 선택이었어요.

e|in hindsight.text: In hindsight, I realize I could have handled that conversation better.
e|in hindsight.en: Thinking back, I understand that I could have managed that conversation in a better way.
e|in hindsight.ko: 지나고 보니 그 대화를 더 잘 처리할 수 있었던 것 같아요.

e|in the end.text: In the end, we all went home together.
e|in the end.en: Finally, we all went home together.
e|in the end.ko: 결국 우리는 모두 함께 집에 갔어요.

e|in the end.text: She finished her work in the end.
Did you like the movie in the end?
e|in the end.en: Did you finally like the movie?

e|in the long run.text: If you save a little money every month, it pays off in the long run.
e|in the long run.en: Saving a little money each month is helpful over time.
e|in the long run.ko: 매달 조금씩 저축하면 시간이 지나면 도움이 돼요.

e|in the long run.text: Eating healthy might be hard now, but it's better for you in the long run.
e|in the long run.en: Eating healthy food now is better for your health over time.
e|in the long run.ko: 지금은 건강하게 먹는 것이 힘들 수 있지만, 시간이 지나면 더 좋아요.

e|in the long run.text: Skipping sleep is not great in the long run.
e|in the long run.en: Not getting enough sleep is not good after a long time.
e|in the long run.ko: 잠을 못 자는 것은 시간이 지나면 좋지 않아요.

e|it depends.text: Can we go to the park today? It depends on the weather.
e|it depends.en: We can go to the park if the weather is good.
e|it depends.ko: 오늘 공원에 갈 수 있는지는 날씨에 따라 달라요.

e|it depends.text: Will you help me move? It depends if I finish work early.
e|it depends.en: I will help you move if I finish work early.
e|it depends.ko: 내가 일을 일찍 끝내면 도와줄 수 있어요.

e|it depends.text: Are we having pizza tonight? It depends what everyone wants.
e|it depends.en: We will have pizza if everyone wants it.

e|it must have been.text: It must have been difficult to move to a new city alone.
e|it must have been.en: It was probably hard for you to move to a new city by yourself.
e|it must have been.ko: 혼자서 새로운 도시로 이사하는 것은 아마 힘들었을 거예요.

e|it must have been.text: Wow, it must have been amazing to see the northern lights!
e|it must have been.en: I'm sure seeing the northern lights was wonderful for you.
e|it must have been.ko: 와, 오로라를 보는 것은 정말 멋졌겠어요!

e|it must have been.text: It must have been noisy living near the train station.
e|it must have been.en: Living close to the train station was probably loud.

e|it seems to me.text: It seems to me that we should leave a bit earlier to avoid traffic.
e|it seems to me.en: I think we should leave a bit earlier to avoid traffic.
e|it seems to me.ko: 우리는 교통 체증을 피하기 위해 좀 더 일찍 출발해야 할 것 같아.

e|it seems to me.text: It seems to me you’re not really interested in going to the party tonight.
e|it seems to me.en: I think you’re not really interested in going to the party tonight.
e|it seems to me.ko: 오늘 밤 파티에 가는 데 너는 별로 관심이 없는 것 같아.

e|it seems to me.text: It seems to me that this movie is too long for kids to enjoy.
e|it seems to me.en: I think this movie is too long for kids to enjoy.
e|it seems to me.ko: 이 영화는 아이들이 즐기기엔 너무 긴 것 같아.

e|it turned out.text: It turned out she forgot her keys at home.
e|it turned out.en: She did not bring her keys because she left them at home.
e|it turned out.ko: 그녀는 집에 열쇠를 두고 와서 가져오지 않았다.

e|it turned out.text: It turned out to be a sunny day after all.
e|it turned out.en: In the end, the day was sunny.

e|it turned out.text: It turned out the store was closed.
e|it turned out.en: We found that the store was not open.

e|it was fun.text: We played outside and it was fun.
e|it was fun.en: We played outside and we enjoyed it.

e|it was fun.text: Did you think it was fun?
Thank you for coming, it was fun.
e|it was fun.en: Thank you for coming, I enjoyed it.

e|it's hard to say.text: It's hard to say if we'll finish on time.
e|it's hard to say.en: We can't be sure if we will finish on time.
e|it's hard to say.ko: 우리가 제시간에 끝낼 수 있을지 확실하지 않다.

e|it's hard to say.text: It's hard to say what she really meant.
e|it's hard to say.en: It's difficult to know what she truly meant.
e|it's hard to say.ko: 그녀가 진짜로 무엇을 의미했는지 알기 어렵다.

e|it's hard to say.text: It's hard to say which one is better.
e|it's hard to say.en: It's not easy to decide which one is better.
e|it's hard to say.ko: 어느 것이 더 나은지 결정하기 어렵다.

e|it's not worth it.text: I wanted to argue, but honestly, it's not worth it.
e|it's not worth it.en: I wanted to argue, but honestly, it's not important enough to bother.
e|it's not worth it.ko: 나는 논쟁하고 싶었지만, 솔직히 그럴 가치가 없어.

e|it's not worth it.text: If the movie is boring, let's leave—it's not worth it.
e|it's not worth it.en: If the movie is boring, let's leave because it's not good enough to stay.
e|it's not worth it.ko: 영화가 지루하면 나가자, 그럴 가치가 없어.

e|it's not worth it.text: Why stay up all night worrying? It's not worth it.
e|it's not worth it.en: Why stay up all night worrying? It's not important enough to do that.
e|it's not worth it.ko: 밤새 걱정할 필요 없어, 그럴 가치가 없어.

e|it's up to you.text: We can watch a movie or play a game, it's up to you.
e|it's up to you.en: You can choose if we watch a movie or play a game.
e|it's up to you.ko: 영화를 볼지 게임을 할지 네가 선택해.

e|it's up to you.text: It's up to you how you want to decorate your room.
e|it's up to you.en: You can decide how you want to decorate your room.
e|it's up to you.ko: 네 방을 어떻게 꾸밀지는 네가 정해.

e|it's up to you.text: We can leave now or stay a bit longer, it's up to you.
e|it's up to you.en: We can leave now or stay a bit longer, you decide.
e|it's up to you.ko: 지금 나갈지 좀 더 있을지 네가 정해.

e|it's worth trying.text: If you are not sure, it's worth trying.
e|it's worth trying.en: If you are not sure, you should try it.

e|it's worth trying.text: This new app looks fun, it's worth trying.
e|it's worth trying.en: This new app looks fun, so you should try it.
e|it's worth trying.ko: 이 새 앱은 재미있어 보여, 시도해 볼 만해.

e|it's worth trying.text: I know it's hard, but it's worth trying.
e|it's worth trying.en: I know it's hard, but you should still try it.
e|it's worth trying.ko: 힘든 거 알지만 시도해 볼 만해.

e|just in case.text: Take an umbrella just in case it rains.
e|just in case.en: Bring an umbrella to be prepared if it rains.
e|just in case.ko: 비가 올 경우를 대비해서 우산을 가져가.

e|just in case.text: I saved your number just in case I need to call you.
e|just in case.en: I kept your number so I can call you if needed.
e|just in case.ko: 혹시 전화해야 할 일이 생길까 봐 네 번호를 저장했어.

e|just in case.text: Let’s leave early just in case there is traffic.
e|just in case.en: Let's go early to avoid problems if there is traffic.
e|just in case.ko: 교통 체증이 있을 경우를 대비해서 일찍 출발하자.

e|just this one.text: Can I have just this one?
I need just this one spoon.
Please take just this one bag.

e|keep in touch.text: Let’s keep in touch after the trip.
e|keep in touch.en: Let’s talk to each other after the trip.

e|keep in touch.text: Keep in touch so I know you’re safe.
e|keep in touch.en: Stay in contact so I know you are safe.
e|keep in touch.ko: 네가 안전한지 알 수 있도록 연락해.

e|keep in touch.text: It was nice meeting you, keep in touch!
e|keep in touch.en: It was good to meet you, let’s contact each other again!

e|last night.text: I saw a cat in the yard last night.
e|last night.en: I saw a cat in the yard yesterday when it was dark.

e|last night.text: Did you hear the storm last night?
e|last night.en: Did you hear the storm that happened yesterday at night?

e|last night.text: We had pizza for dinner last night.
e|last night.en: We ate pizza for dinner yesterday in the evening.

e|let me check.text: Let me check if the bus is here.
e|let me check.en: I will see if the bus has arrived.

e|let me check.text: Let me check my bag for your pen.
e|let me check.en: I will look in my bag for your pen.

e|let me check.text: Let me check what time the movie starts.
e|let me check.en: I will find out when the movie begins.

e|let me know.text: Let me know if you need more time.
e|let me know.en: Tell me if you need more time.

e|let me know.text: Let me know when you get home.
e|let me know.en: Tell me when you arrive at your home.

e|let me know.text: Let me know what you think about this.
e|let me know.en: Tell me your opinion about this.
e|let me know.ko: 이것에 대해 어떻게 생각하는지 알려 주세요.

e|let's meet at.text: Let's meet at the park after school.
e|let's meet at.en: We can see each other at the park when school is done.

e|let's meet at.text: Let's meet at the bus stop in the morning.
e|let's meet at.en: We can see each other at the bus stop in the morning.

e|let's meet at.text: Let's meet at your house before lunch.
e|let's meet at.en: We can see each other at your house before eating lunch.
e|let's meet at.ko: 점심 먹기 전에 네 집에서 만나자.

e|make a decision.text: It's hard to make a decision when both options seem good.
e|make a decision.en: It's difficult to choose when both choices look good.
e|make a decision.ko: 두 선택지가 모두 좋아 보여서 결정하기가 어렵다.

e|make a decision.text: Let me know when you make a decision about dinner.
e|make a decision.en: Tell me your choice about what to eat for dinner when you decide.

e|make a decision.text: Sometimes you just have to make a decision and move on.
e|make a decision.en: Sometimes you just need to choose and then continue with your life.
e|make a decision.ko: 가끔은 그냥 결정을 내리고 넘어가야 해.

e|make sure.text: Please make sure you lock the door.
e|make sure.en: Please check the door is locked.

e|make sure.text: Make sure you bring your umbrella today.
e|make sure.en: Remember to bring your umbrella today.

e|make sure.text: Make sure you turn off the lights before you leave.
e|make sure.en: Be certain to turn off the lights before you go out.
e|make sure.ko: 나가기 전에 불을 끄는 것을 꼭 확인해.

e|maybe next time.text: Sorry, maybe next time we can play together.
e|maybe next time.en: Sorry, we can play together another time.
e|maybe next time.ko: 미안해, 다음에 같이 놀 수 있을 거야.

e|maybe next time.text: I cannot go to the park, maybe next time.
e|maybe next time.en: I cannot go to the park, another time maybe.

e|maybe next time.text: Can I join your game? Maybe next time.
e|maybe next time.en: Can I join your game? Not this time, but another time.
e|maybe next time.ko: 너희 게임에 나도 껴도 돼? 이번에는 안 되고 다음에 하자.

e|me too.text: I want ice cream, me too.

e|meet halfway.text: Can we meet halfway on the price?
e|meet halfway.en: Can we compromise on the price?

e|meet halfway.text: If you can meet halfway, I’ll help you move.
e|meet halfway.en: If you can compromise, I’ll help you move.

e|meet halfway.text: Let’s meet halfway and choose a restaurant we both like.
e|meet halfway.en: Let’s compromise and choose a restaurant we both like.

e|more or less.text: The meeting went more or less as we expected.
e|more or less.en: The meeting happened mostly as we thought it would.
e|more or less.ko: 회의가 우리가 예상한 대로 거의 진행됐어.

e|more or less.text: I understand what you mean, more or less.
e|more or less.en: I mostly understand what you are saying.
e|more or less.ko: 네가 무슨 말 하는지 대충 알겠어.

e|needless to say.text: Needless to say, you should bring an umbrella if it looks like rain.
e|needless to say.en: Obviously, you should bring an umbrella if it looks like rain.
e|needless to say.ko: 비가 올 것 같으면 우산을 가져가는 게 당연해요.

e|needless to say.text: Needless to say, everyone was excited when the concert tickets sold out so quickly.
e|needless to say.en: Of course, everyone was excited when the concert tickets were all gone so fast.
e|needless to say.ko: 콘서트 티켓이 그렇게 빨리 매진되자 모두가 신난 건 당연했어요.

e|needless to say.text: Needless to say, finishing your homework before watching TV is a good idea.
e|needless to say.en: Obviously, it's smart to finish your homework before watching TV.
e|needless to say.ko: TV 보기 전에 숙제를 끝내는 게 좋은 생각인 건 말할 필요도 없어요.

e|next to the bank.text: The bus stop is next to the bank.
e|next to the bank.en: The bus stop is beside the bank.

e|next to the bank.text: There is a flower shop next to the bank.
e|next to the bank.en: There is a flower shop beside the bank.

e|next to the bank.text: Let’s meet next to the bank.
e|next to the bank.en: Let us meet beside the bank.

e|next weekend.text: I will see my grandma next weekend.
e|next weekend.en: I plan to visit my grandma next weekend.
e|next weekend.ko: 나는 다음 주말에 할머니를 볼 거예요.

e|next weekend.en: Let's go for a hike next weekend.

e|next weekend.text: We can clean the house next weekend.
e|next weekend.en: We can tidy the house next weekend.
e|next weekend.ko: 우리는 다음 주말에 집을 청소할 수 있어.

e|nice to meet you.en: Hello, it is good to see you for the first time.

e|nice to meet you.text: Hi, nice to meet you. I am new here.
e|nice to meet you.en: Hi, I am glad to meet you. I just arrived.
e|nice to meet you.ko: 안녕, 만나서 반가워요. 저 여기 처음이에요.

e|nice to meet you.text: Nice to meet you, my name is Kim.
e|nice to meet you.en: I am happy to see you for the first time, my name is Kim.
e|nice to meet you.ko: 처음 뵙게 되어 반가워요, 제 이름은 김이에요.

e|no problem.text: Thank you for the book. No problem.
e|no problem.en: Thanks for the book. It is fine.

e|no problem.text: Sorry, I am late. No problem.
e|no problem.en: It is okay that you are late.

e|no problem.text: Can I use your pen? No problem.
e|no problem.en: Yes, you can use my pen. That is okay.
e|no problem.ko: 네, 제 펜 써도 돼요. 괜찮아요.

e|no way.text: No way, you finished that huge pizza by yourself?
e|no way.en: I can't believe you ate that whole pizza alone.
e|no way.ko: 너 혼자서 그 큰 피자를 다 먹었다니 믿을 수 없어.

e|no way.text: No way, I just saw your lost keys on the counter!
e|no way.en: I can't believe I found your lost keys on the counter.
e|no way.ko: 네가 잃어버린 열쇠를 카운터에서 찾다니 믿을 수 없어.

e|no way.text: No way am I going outside in this storm.
e|no way.en: I'm definitely not going outside because of this storm.
e|no way.ko: 이런 폭풍우에 나는 절대 밖에 나가지 않을 거야.

e|no wonder.text: No wonder you look tired, you worked all night.
e|no wonder.en: It is easy to understand why you look tired because you worked all night.
e|no wonder.ko: 네가 피곤해 보이는 것이 당연해, 밤새 일했으니까.

e|no wonder.text: No wonder it is so cold, the window is open.
e|no wonder.en: It makes sense that it is very cold because the window is open.
e|no wonder.ko: 이렇게 추운 게 당연해, 창문이 열려 있으니까.

e|no wonder.text: No wonder the soup tastes bad, there is too much salt.
e|no wonder.en: It is not surprising that the soup tastes bad because there is too much salt.
e|no wonder.ko: 수프 맛이 없는 게 당연해, 소금이 너무 많으니까.

e|not bad at all.text: Your drawing is not bad at all.
This soup tastes not bad at all.
For a rainy day, it's not bad at all.
e|not bad at all.en: It is pretty good for a rainy day.

e|not really.text: Not really, I am just tired.
Not really. I would rather stay in.
e|not really.en: No. I prefer to stay home.

e|not to mention.text: The hike was long and tiring, not to mention really muddy at the end.
e|not to mention.en: The hike was long and tiring, and it was also very muddy at the end.
e|not to mention.ko: 하이킹이 길고 힘들었고, 끝에는 정말 진흙투성이였다.

e|not to mention.text: The rent is expensive, not to mention how much utilities cost here.
e|not to mention.en: The rent is expensive, and the utilities cost a lot too.
e|not to mention.ko: 집세가 비싼데, 여기서는 공과금도 많이 든다.

e|not to mention.text: It was cold outside, not to mention it started raining halfway through the game.
e|not to mention.en: It was cold outside, and it also started raining in the middle of the game.
e|not to mention.ko: 밖이 추웠고, 경기 도중에 비까지 오기 시작했다.

e|on the fence.text: I'm still on the fence about joining the gym this month.
e|on the fence.en: I haven't decided yet if I want to join the gym this month.
e|on the fence.ko: 이번 달에 헬스장에 등록할지 아직 결정하지 못했어.

e|on the fence.text: She's on the fence about accepting the new job offer.
e|on the fence.en: She hasn't decided yet if she will accept the new job offer.
e|on the fence.ko: 그녀는 새 일자리 제안을 받아들일지 아직 결정하지 못했어.

e|on the fence.text: I'm on the fence between ordering pizza or sushi for dinner.
e|on the fence.en: I can't decide between ordering pizza or sushi for dinner.
e|on the fence.ko: 저녁으로 피자를 시킬지 스시를 시킬지 결정하지 못하고 있어.

e|on the left.text: The red bag is on the left.
e|on the left.en: The red bag is in the place to the left side.

e|on the left.text: Sit on the left of me.
e|on the left.en: Sit in the place to my left side.

e|on the left.text: Is the store on the left?
e|on the left.en: Is the store in the place to the left side?

e|on the other hand.text: I like living in the city, but on the other hand, the countryside is much quieter.
e|on the other hand.en: I like living in the city, but the countryside is much quieter.
e|on the other hand.ko: 나는 도시에서 사는 것이 좋지만, 한편 시골은 훨씬 조용해.

e|on the other hand.text: The movie was a bit long, but on the other hand, the story was really interesting.
e|on the other hand.en: The movie was a bit long, but the story was really interesting.
e|on the other hand.ko: 영화가 좀 길었지만, 한편 이야기는 정말 흥미로웠어.

e|on the other hand.text: On the one hand, I want to save money, but on the other hand, I need a new phone.
e|on the other hand.en: I want to save money, but I need a new phone.
e|on the other hand.ko: 나는 돈을 아끼고 싶지만, 한편 새 휴대폰이 필요해.

e|on the way.text: The pizza is on the way.
The rain is on the way.
Is your friend on the way?

e|on time.text: The bus is never on time.
e|on time.en: The bus always comes late or early, not at the right time.

e|on time.text: Please try to finish your work on time.
e|on time.en: Please try to complete your work by the deadline.

e|on time.text: Will the food be ready on time?
e|on time.en: Will the food be ready when it should be?

e|out of the question.text: Going out in this storm is out of the question.
e|out of the question.en: It is not possible to go out in this storm.

e|out of the question.text: Staying up all night before the exam is out of the question for me.
e|out of the question.en: I cannot stay up all night before the exam.
e|out of the question.ko: 시험 전날 밤을 새우는 것은 나에게 불가능해요.

e|out of the question.text: Is taking a week off work out of the question right now?
e|out of the question.en: Is it impossible to take a week off work right now?
e|out of the question.ko: 지금 일주일 휴가를 내는 것은 불가능한가요?

e|read between the lines.text: Sometimes you have to read between the lines to get the full story.
e|read between the lines.en: Sometimes you need to look carefully to understand the whole story.
e|read between the lines.ko: 가끔은 전체 이야기를 이해하려면 자세히 살펴봐야 해.

e|read between the lines.text: If you read between the lines, you'll realize she's actually upset.
e|read between the lines.en: If you understand what is not directly said, you'll realize she's actually upset.
e|read between the lines.ko: 겉으로 드러나지 않은 말을 이해하면 그녀가 사실 화났다는 걸 알 수 있어.

e|read between the lines.text: You really need to read between the lines with his emails.
e|read between the lines.en: You really need to understand what is implied in his emails.
e|read between the lines.ko: 그의 이메일에서는 숨겨진 의미를 파악해야 해.

e|run out of.text: We will run out of milk if we don't buy more.
e|run out of.en: We will have no more milk if we do not buy more.
e|run out of.ko: 우리가 더 사지 않으면 우유가 다 떨어질 거야.

e|run out of.text: Did you run out of paper for the printer?
e|run out of.en: Do you have no more paper for the printer?

e|run out of.text: My phone will run out of battery soon.
e|run out of.en: My phone will have no power soon.
e|run out of.ko: 내 핸드폰 배터리가 곧 다 닳을 거야.

e|say that again.text: It is loud here, say that again.
e|say that again.en: It is noisy, please repeat what you said.

e|say that again.ko: 방금 말한 것을 다시 말해 주세요.

e|see you later.text: I have to go now, see you later.
e|see you later.en: I have to leave now, goodbye for now.
e|see you later.ko: 나 이제 가야 해, 나중에 봐.

e|see you later.text: See you later, have a good day!
e|see you later.en: Goodbye for now, enjoy your day!

e|see you later.text: See you later at the park.
e|see you later.en: Goodbye for now, we will meet at the park.

e|see you then.text: The movie starts at seven, see you then.
e|see you then.en: We will meet when the movie starts at seven.
e|see you then.ko: 영화가 일곱 시에 시작하니까 그때 보자.

e|see you then.text: Dinner is at my place on Friday, see you then.
e|see you then.en: We will meet at my house for dinner on Friday.
e|see you then.ko: 금요일에 내 집에서 저녁 먹으니까 그때 보자.

e|see you then.text: Class ends at three, see you then.
e|see you then.en: We will meet when class ends at three.
e|see you then.ko: 수업이 세 시에 끝나니까 그때 보자.

e|should have known.text: I should have known the meeting was canceled when nobody showed up.
e|should have known.en: I made a mistake not realizing the meeting was canceled when no one came.
e|should have known.ko: 아무도 오지 않았을 때 회의가 취소된 걸 알아챘어야 했어요.

e|should have known.text: You should have known it would rain today with those dark clouds.
e|should have known.en: It was obvious it would rain because the sky was full of dark clouds.
e|should have known.ko: 저렇게 먹구름이 많은데 오늘 비가 올 걸 알았어야 했어요.

e|should have known.text: She should have known that her keys were in her bag the whole time.
e|should have known.en: She made a mistake not realizing her keys were always in her bag.
e|should have known.ko: 그녀는 열쇠가 내내 가방 안에 있었다는 걸 알아챘어야 했어요.

e|so far.text: So far, the weather has been nice.
e|so far.en: Until now, the weather has been nice.

e|so far.text: How is your project going so far?
e|so far.en: How has your project gone until now?

e|so far.text: We have no news so far.
e|so far.en: We have not received any news until now.

e|sort it out.text: Let’s sort it out after lunch.
e|sort it out.en: We will fix the problem after lunch.

e|sort it out.text: Don’t worry, we can sort it out together.
e|sort it out.en: Do not worry, we can fix it together.
e|sort it out.ko: 걱정하지 마, 우리 함께 해결할 수 있어.

e|sort it out.text: I will talk to him and sort it out.
e|sort it out.en: I will speak to him and fix the problem.

e|sounds good.text: We can meet at the park at five, sounds good.
e|sounds good.en: Meeting at the park at five is okay for me.
e|sounds good.ko: 다섯 시에 공원에서 만나는 거 좋아요.

e|sounds good.text: Let’s try that new cafe for lunch, sounds good.
e|sounds good.en: Going to the new cafe for lunch is a good idea.
e|sounds good.ko: 점심으로 새 카페에 가는 거 좋네요.

e|sounds good.text: If you want to watch a movie tonight, sounds good.
e|sounds good.en: Watching a movie tonight is fine with me.
e|sounds good.ko: 오늘 밤에 영화 보는 거 괜찮아요.

e|take into account.text: We should take into account the weather before making any plans.
e|take into account.en: We need to think about the weather before we decide what to do.
e|take into account.ko: 우리가 무엇을 할지 정하기 전에 날씨도 고려해야 해.
